elements.quote: An overall and cumulative meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate and quantify this efficacy.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the report as an overall and cumulative meta-analysis (systematic review with meta-analysis).

elements.quote: Objectives: An overall and cumulative meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate and quantify this efficacy.
elements.reason: The abstract states the main objective / review question: to evaluate and quantify the efficacy of acupuncture for Bell's palsy.
The abstract does not specify the main inclusion or exclusion criteria (participants, interventions, comparators, outcomes, study designs) in the provided text.

elements.quote: Searches of PubMed, EMBASE, Wanfang data - base and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were performed up to July 2016,
elements.reason: The abstract identifies the information sources searched and reports the date up to which searches were performed (July 2016).
The abstract does not report the methods used to assess risk of bias in included studies (no mention of tools or assessment procedures).

elements.quote: Study appraisal and synthesis methods: Searches ... and a random-effect model was used to yield summary relative risks (RRs).
elements.reason: The abstract states the synthesis method used (random-effects model) and the effect measure (relative risks), describing how results were pooled.
The abstract does not report the total number of included studies or participants nor summarize key study characteristics in the provided text.

elements.quote: Results: Compared to conventional treatments, RRs for total effective rate and cured rate of acupuncture are 1.11 (95% confidence interval (CI)=1.05-1.17) and 1.56 (95% CI=1.30 - 1.87), respectively.
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcomes (effect estimates and CIs) for total effective rate and cured rate.

elements.quote: RRs for total effective rate and cured rate of acupuncture are 1.11 (95% confidence interval (CI)=1.05-1.17) and 1.56 (95% CI=1.30 - 1.87), respectively.
elements.reason: A meta-analysis was conducted and the abstract reports the summary estimates with 95% confidence intervals.

elements.quote: Compared to conventional treatments, RRs for total effective rate and cured rate of acupuncture are 1.11 ... and 1.56 ...
elements.reason: The abstract compares acupuncture to conventional treatments and reports effect estimates >1, indicating the direction of effect (favoring acupuncture for the reported outcomes).

elements.quote: Conclusion: In conclusion, we failed to draw a conclusion that the acupuncture is effective for facial paralysis since these limited methodological quality studies and potential biases, there need to be validated by more well designed and large sample size RCTs.
elements.reason: The abstract briefly summarizes important limitations of the included evidence (limited methodological quality and potential biases).

elements.quote: Conclusion: In conclusion, we failed to draw a conclusion that the acupuncture is effective for facial paralysis ... there need to be validated by more well designed and large sample size RCTs.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and an implication: that current evidence is insufficient and more well-designed large RCTs are needed.
The abstract does not state the primary source of funding for the review.
The abstract does not provide any registration information (registry name or registration number).

No explicit statement of the review objectives or research questions was located in the supplied evidence (no abstract or introduction text specifying objectives or using a question-formulation framework).

Although the review evaluates an intervention (acupuncture), the supplied evidence does not state planned comparisons using PICO or a similar framework; no explicit PICO elements or planned comparison statement were found.

elements.quote: Two investigators (Fu-ming Wang and Sha-sha Yu) independently selected the suitable publications according to following inclusion criteria: (1) Participants: subjects diagnosed with Bell's palsy. (2) Intervention: manual acupuncture or electric acupuncture. (3) Control: other therapy regimens except acupuncture. (4) Outcome: Adjusted risk estimates with 95% confidence interval (CI) on the association of acupuncture and efficacy of Bell's palsy included cured rate and effective rate. (5) Study design: RCTs. The criteria were determined with reference to the House-Brackmann judging and grading system of facial nerve function.
elements.reason: The chunk lists participant eligibility, interventions, controls, outcomes, and eligible study design, and notes use of House-Brackmann for outcome definitions.

elements.quote: Systematic literature searches of PubMed, EMBASE, Wanfang database and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were conducted up to July 2016. ... No attempt was made to identify unpublished reports.
elements.reason: The review reports the search date range and explicitly states they did not attempt to identify unpublished reports (publication status), but it does not explicitly state eligibility restrictions by language or dissemination year as part of the inclusion criteria.
No evidence was found distinguishing exclusions because outcomes were not measured from exclusions because outcome results were not reported.

elements.quote: Eleven studies compared acupuncture against other interventions: nine RCTs used drug therapy as a control; one RCT used Chinese traditional manipulation [41]; one RCT used stellate ganglion block therapy as a control [47]. In addition, nine studies [29-31, 33, 35, 36, 39, 40, 48] compared acupuncture plus other interventions against drug therapy: seven RCTs used acupuncture plus drug therapy against drug therapy; one RCT used acupuncture plus HeNe laser radiation against drug therapy [35]; one RCT used acupuncture plus moxibustion against drug therapy [40].
elements.reason: The review specifies the groups used in analyses (acupuncture vs various controls; acupuncture plus other interventions vs drug therapy), linking these groupings to the comparisons synthesized.
No explicit rationale is provided for notable eligibility restrictions (e.g., restricting to RCTs or excluding unpublished reports) beyond stating the criteria; no justification text was identified.

elements.quote: In this meta-analysis, relative risk (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) was considered as common measure of the association between acupuncture therapy and total effective rate or total cured rate. elements.reason: The methods explicitly state that relative risk (RR) with 95% CI was used as the effect measure for the specified outcomes (total effective rate and total cured rate) and that pooled RRs were obtained using a random-effects model.

There is no explanation or justification provided for the choice of effect measure (RR) beyond stating it was used; no rationale or discussion of why RR was chosen over other measures is present in the supplied text.

elements.quote: All the selected 20 studies were used to calculate the pooled estimate for assessing the total effective rate. elements.reason: The manuscript specifies which studies were included in each synthesis (e.g. 20 studies for total effective rate, 15 RCTs for cured rate) and describes inclusion criteria for study selection (participants, interventions, controls, outcomes, study design in text_3) as well as subgroup stratification variables used to decide study groupings for subgroup syntheses (age, contrast design, acupuncture design, sample size, therapy period, disease stage in text_5).

The Methods / Data Synthesis text describes the effect measure used (RR with 95% CI), the pooling model (random-effects), heterogeneity assessment, subgroup, sensitivity and cumulative analyses, and that authors were contacted if necessary, but it does not describe any methods for preparing collected data for presentation or synthesis such as handling missing summary statistics, imputations, conversions between effect measures, or specific data transformation rules.

elements.quote: The following information was extracted: first author, publication year, study location, sample size, mean age, disease stage.
